R27A BK3 Installed 3
Recently, we purchased a few of these low-cost E1.S and E3.S PCIe adapters that can be found on Amazon and AliExpress. For about $60, you can get an adapter with a fan to fit an EDSFF drive into a PCIe slot. Still, we had a question of how well these actually worked. We purchased the fan versions because we were not confident we could get enough airflow through the bare units.
You can find what we purchased on Amazon (affiliate link) or AliExpress (Affiliate link.) There are different versions, including a U.2 version, so make sure you are buying the correct model.
ADT R27A-BK3 EDSFF E1.S and E3.S to PCIe Slot Review
The card itself is large because it needs to fit an E3.S SSD, a fan, and then a converter board.
R27A BK3 Top 1
Along the top, there is just the metal cover.
R27A BK3 Side 2
The I/O plate is mostly just there to hold the card in place and provide vents for airflow.
R27A BK3 Front 2
On the rear, in Sam’s labeling or what we might call the front if it was installed in a server, you can see we just have screws and then the fan cable. It takes a 4-pin PWM fan connection.
R27A BK3 Rear 2
Here is the bottom edge with the PCIe Gen5 x4 connector. There is a Gen4 version of this, so make sure you are getting the version you need.
R27A BK3 Side 1
Taking off the cover takes a few screws and then we can see what is inside.
R27A BK3 Inside 1
First, there is the 4-pin PWM blower fan.
R27A BK3 Fan 1
There is also a PCIe x4 to EDSFF 1C SSD.
R27A BK3 Inside 2
Since it is a shared connector, that means we can install either E1.S or E3.S SSDs into the slot here.
R27A BK3 Inside 3
Next, let us get some drives in the unit so you can see what this looks like.
